item.title: Victor Wembanyama delivers message against Luka Dončić and the Lakers in MVP showdown
item.description: SAN ANTONIO — Mitch Johnson didn’t have much use for his clipboard at the moment. The Spurs head coach sat in the middle of the huddle with a crowd around him, gesturing flagrantly with a 17-point deficit staring his team in the face. No X’s-and-O’s pep talk was necessary; Johnson was demonstrating how his players needed to respond to the Lakers’ force. A message heard by many was truly intended for one very tall alien. On Friday, every step Victor Wembanyama took was met with more resistance than Agent J and Agent K from Men in Black . The men in purple had made it very clear from the opening tip of their intention to rough Wembanyama up. Pressure in the backcourt. Pressure in the frontcourt. Double teams. Fronting him with a second — and sometimes a third — helper rotating over the second his hands touched the ball. The old Wemby might have wilted, faded away as the game wore on, frustrated with the overwhelming physicality. This updated version simply downloads the data and adjusts like artificial intelligence. So the Spurs stormed back in the second half, and with the game hanging in the balance, it was Wembanyama who answered brute force’s call. At one end, the Frenchman barrelled through Luka Dončić and Walker Kessler en route to the rim for an emphatic slam. Seconds later, he darted to the restricted area, leaping as high as his limbs and outstretched fingertips could go, sending Collin Sexton’s shot all the way back to La Brea. Message received. “There was some maturity tonight that was good to see,” Johnson said following the 99-96 win , which earned the Spurs a spot in the NBA Cup quarterfinals . “When things aren’t going well, there are some things you can’t control. But I thought we did a good job of working the game, staying in the game. It was a good step against a very high-level team.” Friday night — or the latest reboot of Alien vs. Predator — was a celebration of differences. On one hand, this was the apex of Western Conference talent, a showdown of Wembanyama and Dončić, MVP favorites who do their respective damage in contrasting styles and their relationship with space. Dončić, the swashbuckling offensive hub that has mastered the art of manipulating areas around him, against Wembanyama, the defensive wizard who can magnify or minimize game plans on a whim. On the other hand, it was unique insight into Wembanyama’s growth and exactly what sets him apart from his peers. This game was not aesthetically pleasing. No team shot better than 50% from the field, 35% from deep or even 75% from the charity stripe. There were 39 combined turnovers and 32 fouls. Dončić finished with 31 points on 31 shots, Wembanyama ended up with 25 points on 25 shots. But even amidst the ugliness, beauty can be uncovered. The postgame locker room mood suggested as much, with the Spurs fully understanding the Lakers’ unique, aggressive approach to Wembanyama. item.title: Duda Sampaio on Japan friendly: “We’re expecting a great game”
item.description: Duda Sampaio on Japan friendly: “We’re expecting a great game” The Brazilian women's national team faces Japan this Sunday (29) at 1:55 a.m. Brasília time at Edion Peace Wing Stadium in Hiroshima, in the team's penultimate match of the 2026 season. After the final training session before the match, midfielder Duda Sampaio looked ahead to the encounter and highlighted the importance of facing a team familiar with Brazil's approach. “We're really looking forward to it. It's the last national team camp of the year, and we're very aware that the World Cup is getting closer and closer. Japan is a familiar opponent, so I think that's good for us, but they should bring something new. Having faced us several times, they also know our style of play well, so I think they could pose challenges, and that's good for our preparation. We're expecting a great match. These are two very strong teams, but if all goes well, we'll come away with the win,” she said. Brazil's players began arriving in Japan on November 22. Although on-field training began on Wednesday (25), the coaching staff organized a series of activities to help the players adjust more quickly and easily to the time difference and the Japanese climate. Duda gave a positive assessment of the preparation period and highlighted how well the team had used its time. “The adjustment went really well. From the first training sessions, we managed to settle in well and get some rest so that, when we got onto the pitch, we could make the most of our training right away. It was a very productive week. We always have limited time here, so we try to make the most of training sessions and meetings,” she explained. Duda Sampaio during a Brazil training session in Hiroshima Credits: Luciana Vermell/CBF Duda Sampaio was announced as a Corinthians signing in late 2022 and has experienced Arthur Elias's work firsthand ever since. The coach left the São Paulo club in 2023 to take charge of the Brazilian national team, and the midfielder, who had already worked with him, became a regular in the Brazil squad. Having been part of that journey makes the milestone of 50 matches in charge of the team, which the coach will reach this Sunday, all the more special. Duda, who earned her 50th Brazil cap in June 2026, highlighted the relationship they have built over the years and her happiness at being part of the process. “I'm very happy to have followed Arthur's work from Corinthians through to his arrival here. For me, experiencing that was very special. We exchange ideas a lot, and I know his work, his way of thinking and him as a person very well. It's a joy to be able to benefit from that here. He's reaching 50 matches, but I'm sure we'll have many more ahead of us, because we know how seriously he takes his work, and it shows all of Brazil that we're on the right track to achieve our goals,” she concluded. Rodgers accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of not taking his game planning seriously, falling asleep and falling during team meetings, missing some meetings altogether, and even forgetting that he was no longer the coach for the Green Bay Packers, the franchise he and Rodgers won a Super Bowl together with. The Steelers promptly released Rodgers following his comments, and team owner Art Rooney II publicly threw his full support behind McCarthy. item.title: NC State takes down Kansas State, 85-70
item.description: RALEIGH, NC - NOVEMBER 19: Qadence Samuels #2 of the NC State Wolfpack shoots over Johnea Donahue #3 of the Georgetown Hoyas during the college basketball game between the Georgetown Hoyas and the NC State Wolfpack on November 19, 2026 at Reynolds Coliseum in Raleigh, NC. (Photo by Nicholas Faulkner/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The shots were falling for both teams on Friday night, which made for an entertaining back and forth that lasted about three quarters—before NC State finally seized control for good. It wasn’t exactly a defensive clinic for either team, not surprisingly, as both hit the 40-point mark in the first half. Wes Moore wasn’t super thrilled about the effort by his team on defense, but it did make for a fun half to watch. The Pack did get a bit better there in the second half, while Kansas State did not. The Wildcats played zone for the entire evening, mixing up some looks here and there, but mostly sticking with a 2-3 that left such spacious gaps that I’m sure Jim Boeheim was turning over in his grave. Qadence Samuels took advantage by doing her best Paul McNeil impression—she was 6-8 from three, and the team finished 10-15 from outside. As you can tell from that attempt total, NC State did not force the issue from the perimeter against K-State’s zone, mostly because that wasn’t necessary, as getting paint touches was still pretty easy. Zoe Brooks was back on the court for the first time in nearly three weeks and was back to her usual playmaking self, if maybe still a step slow. She had a beautiful dish to Khamil Pierre for a bucket to beat the third quarter horn that was part of an 11-0 run that put Kansas State in the rearview for good. That included the first seven points of the fourth quarter, five of which belonged to Brooks. The Pack ended up leading by double figures for the final nine minutes. Desiree Wooten put together another outstanding performance, scoring 21 points on 8-9 shooting; Khamil Pierre led all scorers with 23 points on 9-15 shooting. Samuels finished with 20. A good result for the Pack against a potential NCAA tournament team (K-State is No. 56 in Torvik), but the big test comes Saturday afternoon against LSU and the evil Mrs. SparkleFeathers.

item.title: Friends, Buckeyes, Lunatic Fringe, it’s time to beat That Team Up North
item.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 19: A member of the Ohio State University Marching Band holds up the "Beat Blue Banana" following a Ohio State Buckeyes touchdown during the fourth quarter of a game against the Kent State Golden Flashes at Ohio Stadium on September 19, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Friends, Buckeyes, Lunatic Fringe, lend me your ears. I come neither to praise Ryan Day nor to bury him. In fact, for the next few hours, I would prefer not to discuss the merits of his continued employment at all, because we have far more pressing business to attend to: beating That Team Up North. Believe me, I am well aware of how frustrating, disappointing, and downright demoralizing this Ohio State football season has been. I have spilled more than my fair share of digital ink lamenting the state of the program, questioning the decisions of its leadership, and wondering what needs to change to get the Buckeyes back to where we all believe they belong. I stand by those sentiments, and I suspect that I will feel just as strongly about them when I wake up on Sunday morning. But Sunday is not today, and there is nothing that you, I, or anyone else outside of that locker room can do between now and the final whistle to address the issues that have plagued this program. So, I am imploring every member of Buckeye Nation to temporarily set aside our perfectly legitimate grievances, suspend our cynicism, and embrace the unbridled, unapologetic, occasionally irrational passion that comes with being a fan in the greatest rivalry in all of sports. For one glorious afternoon, I don’t give a damn about the College Football Playoff, the transfer portal, the athletic department’s organizational structure, or the offensive coordinator’s play-calling tendencies, and I certainly don’t give a damn for the whole state of M*ch*g*n. I care about seeing silver helmets lovingly adorned with Buckeye Leaves knock the ever-loving bejesus out of those revolting winged helmets. I care about hearing the opening notes of “Buckeye Battle Cry,” watching the majestic beauty of “Script Ohio,” and feeling the goosebumps that come with hearing an entire stadium singing “Carmen Ohio” in celebration of a victory over the most dastardly program in all of college football. item.title: Luka Dončić gets in physical confrontation with fan
item.description: Credit: Amazon Prime Video It was a bizarre scene in San Antonio as Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić got into a physical confrontation with a fan seated on the baseline. The Lakers held a 16-point halftime lead against the Spurs in their NBA Cup matchup on Friday night, but San Antonio rallied in the second half for a 99-96 victory. Dončić was visibly frustrated as he shot just 1-13 from downtown. He’s been scoring at such a historic rate this season that his 31 points were five off his season average. After the game was over and Luka was walking to the locker room, he took off his elbow band and threw it at a woman seated on the baseline who appeared to be yelling at him. Dončić then went back for the elbow band and the man seated next to her (presumably her husband or a significant other) then shoved Luka before a horde of people intervened to prevent the situation from escalating further. The camera above the backboard captured it all on the Amazon Prime Video telecast. A fan shoved Luka after he threw his band toward them https://t.co/AKh93Z9QUK — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 28, 2026 Luka Dončić is prone to the occasional outburst and his behavior has drawn criticism over the years at various points throughout his career . But this was a regrettable and bizarre incident that was easily preventable. The first fan was clearly letting Luka have it while walking to the locker room, but Dončić should know better and not engage by throwing anything at her. If he just ignored it, then none of what followed would have happened. Going back for the elbow band he threw was another strange decision. As for the male fan, you can appreciate him standing up for the lady, but there’s no excuse for ever putting your hands on a player. Thankfully it didn’t rise to Malice in the Palace levels or anything, but everyone was in the wrong here. item.title: Red Sox's Triston Casas Could Force Interesting Lineup Decision Amid Return
item.description: Red Sox's Triston Casas Could Force Interesting Lineup Decision Amid Return originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Red Sox have spent years trying to sort out their first base and designated hitter situation, hoping Triston Casas would eventually be the answer. Unfortunately for the Red Sox and Casas, injuries have derailed that a bit. As a result, the Red Sox have had to make moves, landing William Contreras last offseason and signing Jake Bauers this winter. A healthy Casas changes the lineup, especially if he can return to the player that we saw back in 2023. While the injuries certainly haven't helped Casas over the past couple of seasons now, there's no debating how good he was in 2023, hitting 24 home runs, 21 doubles, and driving in 65 runs. He returned to action in a winter ball game in the DR, playing Friday and hitting a grand slam. Casas also has a ton of upside. He has legitimate power in his left-handed bat that could play a big role in a Red Sox lineup as he looks to wrap balls around the Pesky Pole. But instead of this being an issue for the Red Sox and forcing them to figure out what to do with Contreras and Bauers, adding a player with this type of pop would never hurt. Even if the Red Sox want to ease Casas back into the lineup and he only plays about 100 games next season, if he can give the type of power production that we're used to seeing from him, and we all know that he has, the 26-year-old has a big future in Boston. That flexibility also helps Boston with injuries. Casas has missed a ton of time, and the Red Sox can't put all their eggs in one basket. With Bauers and Contreras here, any injury to him wouldn't hurt as much as it would have a couple of years ago. Speaking on Cadena SER’s El Larguero , Jabois discussed Bellingham’s influence and the excitement surrounding his latest performances. The journalist believes the comparison with Zidane is not only rooted in their shared association with Real Madrid, pointing to the unusual way Bellingham combines his physical stature with exceptional technical ability. Bellingham combines physical power with Zidane’s elegance Jabois believes Bellingham’s physical profile is central to the comparisons with the French legend. The midfielder’s height and strength do not restrict his movement or technique, allowing him to control the ball and navigate tight spaces with surprising grace. “Jude Bellingham has a unique quality, and I think that’s where the constant comparisons with Zidane come from. He has a great wingspan, and he’s a very tall and big guy. Bellingham is now being compared to Zinedine Zidane. item.title: Eye of the Tiger: Pivotal position matchups for LSU vs. Arkansas
item.description: KNOXVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 21: DJ Pickett #5 of the LSU Tigers looks on during the second half of the game against the Tennessee Volunteers at Neyland Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Knoxville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images In what felt like the blink of an eye, year 1 under Lane Kiffin is nearly over. The Tigers will travel to Fayetteville on Saturday to face the Razorbacks in the regular season finale. With both teams in the bottom five of the conference, it’s an early 11:45 kickoff on SEC Network. LSU lost their third straight game last week to Tennessee, which dropped them to 6-5 overall and 3-5 in the SEC. It’s been a rough season for Kiffin, to say the least. The loss guaranteed a losing record in conference and requiring a win just to match last season’s mark of 7-5. As for Arkansas, they are also under a first-year head coach. Ryan Silverfield came over from Memphis after spending 6 years as their head coach. The Razorbacks are 4-7 overall and 2-6 in the SEC. Unlike LSU, though, those numbers were expected. Everyone understood that Silverfield was fighting an uphill battle, especially trying to get off of the ground. This is a game that Kiffin simply can’t lose. The vibes around the LSU football program are fairly low, regardless of the patience that he has pleaded for. It hasn’t been that they are losing games, it’s how they’re losing games. But as two touchdown favorites, this game is an absolute must-win for the Tigers or things could get ugly amongst the fans. DJ Pickett/PJ Woodland vs. Chris Marshall If the Hogs stand any chance on Saturday, they’ll have to get their top receiver going. Marshall is, essentially, their entire passing attack. With an impressive 61 receptions for 867 yards, his 86.7 yards per game average is 2nd in the SEC. The next closest is Antonio Jordan with only 319 yards. He leads the conference with 39 receptions for 10-plus yards. Despite Arkansas getting blown out by Texas last week, Marshall still managed to gain 106 yards against a good defense. PJ Woodland spent most of the time opposite of opposing #1 receivers earlier in the year, but as DJ Pickett has gotten more settled as a first time starter on the outside, he has drawn more of those matchups. item.title: "Not a Closed Chapter" - Carlos Forbs Hints at Manchester City Return in Alluding Interview
item.description: "Not a Closed Chapter" - Carlos Forbs Hints at Manchester City Return in Alluding Interview Etihad Stadium scouts are understood to have been sent to Club Brugge’s 3-0 win over RC Lens in the UEFA Champions League last month, where former Manchester City player Forbs scored alongside Hans Vanaken and Joaquin Seys. The winger left Sporting CP to join the City Football Academy in 2015 and spent eight years in east Manchester, despite not making his senior debut under Pep Guardiola. Forbs was primarily utilised in Manchester City ’s U21 side, for whom he made 38 appearances, scored 26 goals and provided 13 assists in a largely impressive spell a step down from the first-team. Additionally, Forbs managed to contribute to 47 goals in 34 appearances in the U18 group, while scoring five and assisting six in seven UEFA Youth League games for the Blues. Forbs ‘isn’t ruling out’ Man City return but isn’t focused on that for now In an interview with Dutch outlet Nieuwsblad , the 22-year-old was asked about a potential return to City in the future. “I’m not ruling anything out," the winger said, as translated and relayed by Sport Witness . "Manchester City isn’t a closed chapter, but I’m not focused on that right now." On City scouts being sent to watch him play, he added: “I block out that kind of noise, even if it’s positive. I don’t need it. Of course, it’s nice that teams are keeping an eye on me, but I know myself when I’m performing well or not.” Forbs currently has a contract valid until 2029 with Brugge, alongside a £20 million transfer value. He also noted that his family won’t have a big say in his next move and will “come along” regardless. The idea of Forbs returning to Manchester City , at face value, would be positive. The winger would provide depth in attacking spaces and provide Enzo Maresca with more options at the top of the pitch. Recent form suggests the absence of Antoine Semenyo has wrecked City’s title charge more than anyone expected, and having Forbs, who can play on either wing, would be proactive. Manchester United and Tottenham had already shown their interest in Forbs in October, according to Italian reports , and he was sought after by clubs across Germany and Spain. At present, there is little movement on the situation, but Forbs’ comments about the unclosed chapter at the Etihad Stadium could tempt City director of football Hugo Viana to assess the likelihood of a reunion.

item.title: Newcastle Ownership Shake-Up Emerges as PIF Seeks Sale
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - MARCH 16: Newcastle United chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan celebrates with the Trophy after winning the Carabao Cup Final between Liverpool and Newcastle United at Wembley Stadium on March 16, 2025 in London, England. (Photo by Marc Atkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund is preparing to dilute its Newcastle United shares by selling up to 25 percent of the club. The Guardian’s Matt Hughes reported that JP Morgan has been appointed to handle the process. That said, don’t panic. Everything points to PIF seeking outside investors only to help finance major infrastructure projects, including the building of a new stadium, instead of simply plotting a slow-cooked exit from Tyniside. PIF currently owns 84 percent of Newcastle, with the Reuben brothers holding the remaining 16 percent. A full 25 percent share issue would therefore significantly dilute PIF’s holding while leaving the Saudi fund as majority owner. PIF would retain 63 percent of NUFC after the sale, with the Reubens keeping their 16 percent and the newcomers owning 21 percent of the club and overtaking the latter in the Magpies power ladder. The development arrives amid ever-growing questions about PIF’s sporting portfolio. The fund already withdrew its support from LIV Golf, sold a stake in Al-Hilal and has reportedly shown willingness to dispose of other sporting assets, namely Newcastle—at least in the mind of some fans and outsiders. Those moves have fueled speculation that Newcastle could eventually be sold outright, but Hughes reported that PIF sources insist the fund “retain[s] a long-term commitment to Newcastle.” Newcastle declined to comment on the report. For now, therefore, the confirmed direction is a potential minority dilution rather than a complete PIF departure, even if the fund’s wider pullback from some sporting investments ensures scrutiny will continue. item.description: Freyr Alexandersson has transformed Rosenborg's fortunes in his short time in charge [Getty Images] Swansea City are close to agreeing a deal to appoint Freyr Alexandersson as their new head coach. The Championship club have been in discussions with Alexandersson's current side Rosenborg over compensation for the 44-year-old. The Swans are now confident Alexandersson will be confirmed as Vitor Matos' permanent successor, although the Icelander is expected to still be in charge of Rosenborg's game against Molde in the Norwegian Eliteserien top flight on Saturday evening. Earlier this week, Alexandersson confirmed that there had been "strong interest from Swansea" and admitted he has found it "overwhelming" to be courted by the Welsh club and the attention it has brought him. Interim boss Ashley Williams will take charge of Swansea for Sunday's south Wales derby at home against Cardiff City, but Alexandersson's appointment could swiftly be confirmed after that. Alexandersson has only been in charge of Rosenborg since June. The Norwegian top-flight club were in relegation danger when he was appointed, but lie fourth with just three games remaining in the season, which concludes in mid-December. Alexandersson previously worked for another Norwegian side, Brann, but was sacked earlier this year after 15 months in charge. Prior to that, he was manager of Belgian side Kortrijk, who are a sister club of Cardiff. Alexandersson 'overwhelmed' by Swansea interest Does another derby moment beckon for Williams? Latest Swansea City news, analysis and fan views Listen to the latest Swansea City interviews, news and discussion on BBC Sounds Alexandersson spent five years as manager of the women's national side in Iceland, while he also had a spell as an assistant with the men's team. He was co-manager of Icelandic club Leiknir Reykjavik for part of his spell in charge of Iceland's women. Alexandersson also had a brief stint on the staff at Qatari side Al-Arabi before making his mark at Lyngby Boldklub, where he was in charge between 2021 and 2024. He helped the former Danish champions back into the top flight and then oversaw a successful fight for safety in their first season at the higher level. item.title: Luka Doncic’s Wristband Throw Sparks Ugly Fan Shove Incident
item.description: Nov 23, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) reacts after not getting a foul call in the second half against the Utah Jazz at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers’ 99-96 loss to the San Antonio Spurs on Friday night already stung. The Lakers blew a 20-point lead, fell out of the NBA Cup with a 2-2 group-play record, and watched the Spurs advance as a wild-card team. What happened in the tunnel afterward made the night worse. As Luka Doncic walked toward the visitors’ locker room at Frost Bank Center, he tossed his white wristband into the front row, a postgame habit he says he does almost every night. A woman seated courtside appeared to say something. Doncic took a few more steps, then doubled back after hearing that she or her companion did not want it. The man sitting next to her picked up the wristband, handed it back, and shoved Doncic with his right hand as Doncic turned to leave. “I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game, and then I heard she or he didn’t want it,” Doncic said afterward. “So I went back to grab it, and he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else.” Video from Amazon Prime’s broadcast and fan angles captured the contact. Jarred Vanderbilt immediately stepped in and pulled Doncic away while Lakers staff and arena security swarmed the area. The male fan was ejected. Doncic, asked whether the man said anything else to him, replied simply, “I don’t know. I just went back.” The incident capped a frustrating night for the six-time All-Star. Doncic finished with a game-high 31 points, eight assists, and six rebounds, but he shot just 1-for-13 from three-point range. The Lakers led by as many as 20 in the second quarter and went into halftime up 54-38 before the Spurs outscored them 61-42 in the second half. Stephon Castle scored 26 points, and Victor Wembanyama added 25 points and 16 rebounds as San Antonio improved to 16-4. A fan SHOVES Luka Doncic after Luka threw something and hit his wife 😳 pic.twitter.com/tJ42TV4YyS — Hater Report (@HaterReport) November 28, 2026 Some circulating clips and social posts claimed Doncic flipped off the woman before tossing the wristband; others described the throw as more of a fling than a casual gift. Doncic framed it as a routine gesture that went sideways once he heard the item was unwanted. The NBA has not yet announced whether either side will face additional discipline. League rules strictly prohibit fans from making physical contact with players, and the entire sequence was captured on multiple cameras. The Lakers (15-4) return to action Sunday in Memphis. The Spurs move on in the NBA Cup with early bragging rights after a second-half surge that erased the deficit and knocked Los Angeles out of the in-season tournament.

The reported asking price suggests Detroit would prefer to receive a combination of NHL-ready talent and future assets rather than settle for a prospect-heavy package simply to resolve the situation before Tuesday’s deadline. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
